chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man marries a woman, then is secluded with her, and closes the door upon her or lowers a curtain, then divorces her, the dowry becomes obligatory, and her seclusion with him is considered as consummation."

key_terms.الصَّدَاقُ: The dowry or bridal gift (mahr) obligatory upon the husband.
key_terms.خَلَاؤُهَا بِهَا: Seclusion of the wife with the husband.

ai.seo_question: Does closing the door count as consummation for the purpose of paying the full dowry upon divorce?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that physical consummation is not strictly required for the full dowry to become obligatory; rather, valid seclusion (khalwah) suffices. This ruling underscores the legal weight of privacy and accessibility in marriage contracts, distinguishing between mere engagement and the actualization of marital rights. It reflects the practical application of Quranic principles regarding financial obligations in divorce scenarios.
